content:
True spiritual friendship is a great help on the way to perfection. It is founded not on natural liking alone, but on the mutual desire to love and serve God. Such friendship is rare, but when it is found it is one of the greatest consolations of the devout life.

Choose your friends carefully. Avoid those who lead you into dissipation or who speak lightly of holy things. Seek rather those who encourage you in virtue, who correct you with charity when you fall, and who rejoice with you in the progress of your soul.

In true friendship there is openness without flattery, correction without bitterness, and silence when speech would be unhelpful. The friends of God help one another by prayer more than by many words. They bear one another's burdens and so fulfill the law of Christ.

If you have such a friend, thank God for the gift. If you have not, do not be troubled; God Himself is the most faithful Friend, and He never fails those who seek Him.
